themes.name: AI Agents & Intelligent Systems
themes.description: Build real-world AI applications using Bifrost by Maxim AI and Tavily. Explore challenges across efficient coding agents, agent benchmarking, autonomous security testing, open-source AI infrastructure, and research automation. Choose one of the six problem statements and develop a working solution that meaningfully integrates both technologies.

problem_statements.name: Build a Coding Agent That Gets the Job Done on the Fewest Tokens
problem_statements.description:
Build an AI coding agent that completes real development tasks while minimizing token consumption and operational costs. The agent must continue working through provider outages, enforce individual spending limits, protect confidential repositories by using local models, and require user approval before performing risky operations such as file writes, shell commands, or Git actions.

The solution should demonstrate efficient and reliable coding workflows without compromising correctness, privacy, or security.

problem_statements.name: Build a Benchmarking Platform for AI Agents, Not Just Models
problem_statements.description:
Build a framework-independent benchmarking platform that evaluates AI agents against identical tasks. The platform must measure task success, execution steps, tool calls, token usage, cost, and completion time across repeated runs.

It should also test how agents respond to failing tools, unavailable models, and misleading instructions, while providing a comparison interface with detailed execution traces to help developers understand agent performance and reliability.

problem_statements.name: Build an Agent That Pentests a Target on Its Own
problem_statements.description:
Build an autonomous AI agent capable of performing authorized penetration testing inside a strictly isolated laboratory environment. The agent must explore permitted targets using real security tools, interpret results, independently decide its next actions, and work toward predefined security objectives.

The solution must strictly respect the provided scope, recover from unsuccessful attempts, and generate actionable security reports containing findings, evidence, severity, and remediation recommendations.

problem_statements.name: Open-Source Bifrost Gateway
problem_statements.description:
Extend the open-source Bifrost gateway with a practical feature that solves a real problem for developers or gateway operators. This could include a plugin, provider integration, caching or routing capability, user interface, or developer tool.

The solution must use supported extension points, work with a standard Bifrost installation, and include clear setup instructions, documentation, and tests. The final contribution should be suitable for consideration as an upstream open-source pull request.

problem_statements.name: Tavily Research Agent
problem_statements.description:
Build an AI-powered research agent that prepares a concise, one-page briefing before a meeting. Given a company or person and a scheduled meeting time, the agent should research relevant developments from the preceding 30 days, including news, launches, hires, and other important updates.

The briefing should provide source-backed findings, useful discussion points, and open questions to help users prepare for meaningful conversations.

problem_statements.name: Build a Stale-Answer Detector for AI Applications
problem_statements.description:
Build an AI-powered verification system that identifies outdated information in LLM-generated answers. The system should detect potentially stale claims involving pricing, API versions, regulations, or company information, re-verify them against live web sources, and provide a freshness score for each claim.

The solution should help users distinguish current, reliable information from potentially outdated AI-generated responses using both Tavily and Bifrost.

phases.name: Problem Statements & Prototype Submission
phases.description:
READ THIS IN FULL **Problem statements go live on 1 Nov**, and the **prototype submission window opens at the same time**. Choose your challenge, build your AI-powered solution, and submit your working prototype within the two-week building window.
*Project Submission Instructions*

Select your primary problem statement from the Theme dropdown.

You can build a project using Bifrost by Maxim AI, Tavily, or **both** technologies together. However, you are also allowed to submit 2 separate projects on the 2 technologies.

If you're building a merged project that addresses a Bifrost challenge along with a Tavily challenge, select the Bifrost challenge as your primary problem statement and use the optional Tavily integration checkbox to indicate the additional challenge.

**If you're building only a Tavily project, simply select the relevant Tavily problem statement as your primary theme.**
**And if you're submitting for both the technologies**, make sure that you go ahead and submit the provided submission form in full, providing the details for both the projects.

Your GitHub repository must be public and include a detailed README covering your project, installation steps, implementation, and technologies used.

Your pitch deck should explain the problem, your solution, technical architecture, and working prototype. If you've combined both technologies, clearly demonstrate how each contributes to your project.

A deployed application is not mandatory, but you're welcome to share a live demo or demonstration video.

faq.question: Can I participate individually?
faq.answer: Yes, you can participate individually or with a team of 4.

faq.question: Who can participate in the hackathon?
faq.answer: Students, engineers, developers, AI builders, working professionals, and anyone interested in building solutions can participate.

faq.question: When will the problem statements be released?
faq.answer: The official problem statements will go live on 1 Nov 2026. You can start preparing with your team before then, but the official challenges will be revealed on 1 Nov.

faq.question: Do I need to join Discord?
faq.answer: Yes. Joining the official Discord server is required for all participants. Discord will be used for important announcements, team communication, workshops, challenge updates, technical guidance, and hackathon support.

faq.question: Can I use existing code, libraries, or AI tools?
faq.answer: Yes. You can use existing libraries, frameworks, boilerplate, open-source software, APIs, and AI development tools. However, the core project should be substantially developed during the hackathon.

faq.question: Where can I find the problem statements?
faq.answer: Visit https://hackculture.io/hackathons/ai-global-hackathon and navigate to the Themes section. You'll find six problem statements: four from Bifrost by Maxim AI and two from Tavily. Click Read more to explore each challenge and its requirements.

faq.question: Is it mandatory to use both Bifrost and Tavily?
faq.answer: No. You can build a project using only Bifrost, only Tavily, or combine both technologies into a single project. We're excited to see how creativelyNo. You can build a project using on participants can bring both technologies together.

faq.question: Can I combine two problem statements into one project?
faq.answer:
Yes! You can select a Bifrost problem statement and integrate concepts from a Tavily problem statement into the same project.

For example, you could build an AI coding agent using Bifrost and integrate Tavily to retrieve live technical documentation or verify information.

Your project should meaningfully demonstrate the technologies used, and your README and pitch deck should explain the integration.

faq.question: How do I select my problem statement when submitting?
faq.answer:
In your HackCulture submission form, select your primary problem statement from the dropdown.

If you're building a Bifrost project that also addresses a Tavily challenge, select the Bifrost problem statement as your primary challenge and tick the relevant Tavily challenge under the optional integration checkbox.

If you're building a Tavily-only project, simply select your Tavily problem statement as the primary challenge.

faq.question: Can I submit two separate projects?
faq.answer:
The current submission form is designed for one primary project, including integrated projects using both technologies.

If you want to build separate solutions for Bifrost and Tavily, you can do so, but submit each project through its own available submission entry rather than combining two unrelated repositories into one entry.

faq.question: How will the winners be selected?
faq.answer:
Projects will be evaluated based on innovation, technical execution, problem-solving, AI usage, user experience, and scalability.

Bifrost projects will compete for the Maxim AI cash prizes, while Tavily projects will compete for Tavily API credit awards.

Integrated projects that meaningfully use both technologies can be considered for both prize categories. Using both technologies does not automatically guarantee a higher score or a prize.

faq.question: What prizes can I win?
faq.answer:
The Maxim AI / Bifrost track has a $1,000 cash prize pool.

The Tavily track has 50,000 API credits to be distributed among the top three winning projects.

A strong integrated project can compete for both prize categories, subject to the judging results.

faq.question: How can I claim my free Tavily API credits?
faq.answer:
Tavily is providing 8,000 API credits per eligible participant.

1. Visit https://app.tavily.com/home
2. Sign up or log in.
3. Redeem coupon code GEEKROOM2 using Tavily's coupon redemption option.
4. Verify that the credits have been added to your account.

The coupon is valid until November 28, 2026. These participant credits are separate from the winner prizes.

faq.question: Where do I submit my project?
faq.answer:
Visit https://hackculture.io/hackathons/ai-global-hackathon and log in with your registered account.

Click Manage, navigate to the Submissions tab, and open Problem Statements & Prototype Submission.

Select your problem statement, enter your project title, add your public GitHub repository URL, upload your PPT, and optionally provide a demo video link. Click Save to complete the submission.

faq.question: What should my GitHub repository and PPT contain?
faq.answer:
Your GitHub repository must be publicly accessible and include your working source code and a README explaining the project, its features, setup instructions, and technologies used.

Your PPT should explain the problem, your proposed solution, technical architecture, implementation, and demonstration of your prototype.

If you're submitting an integrated project, clearly explain how Bifrost and Tavily contribute to your solution.

faq.question: Is a deployed application or demo video mandatory?
faq.answer:
No. A deployed application and demo video are optional. However, your GitHub repository and PPT are required.

Your project should be functional, and your README should provide sufficient instructions for judges to understand and run it.

faq.question: What are the submission deadline and judging dates?
faq.answer:
The prototype submission deadline is November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM.

The final judging round is scheduled for November 29, 2026.

Shortlisted teams will receive further information about their presentations and the judging process through the official communication channels.

rules:
### 1. **Build During the Hackathon**

Projects should be substantially developed during the official hackathon period. Existing libraries, frameworks, boilerplate, and supporting infrastructure may be used, but the **core project** should be created during the hackathon.

### 2. **AI Usage**

Participants are encouraged to use **AI models, agents, APIs, vector databases, frameworks**, and other AI technologies. The use of AI tools should be clearly mentioned in the project submission where applicable.

### 3. **Discord & Official Communication**

All participants are **required to join the official [hackathon Discord server](https://discord.gg/STHG8YQdd)**. Discord will be used for **team communication, important announcements, challenge updates, workshops, technical guidance, and hackathon-related support**.

Participants are responsible for checking the official Discord channels regularly so they do not miss important updates, deadlines, or announcements.

Participants are responsible for checking the official Discord channels regularly so they do not miss important updates, deadlines, or announcements.

### 4. **Team Size**

Teams can consist of **1–4 members**. Each participant can be part of only one team.

### 5. **Original Work**

All submissions must be original work or use components that participants have the legal right to use. *Plagiarism or unauthorized use of intellectual property* will result in disqualification.

### 6. **Third-Party Tools**

Participants may use third-party APIs, SDKs, datasets, open-source software, and developer tools, provided they comply with the applicable *licenses and terms of service*.

### 7. **Submission Requirements**

Each submission must include:
* A **working project or demo**
* Source code or repository
* Project description
* Explanation of the problem being solved
* Technologies and tools used
* **Explanation of how AI is used in the solution**
* Demo video, if required

**Build Resources:**  
Participants can explore the [Bifrost GitHub repository](https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost) as a technical resource while building their projects.

### 8. **One Submission per Team**

Each team may submit **only one final project**.

### 9. **Responsible Development**

Projects must comply with applicable laws and platform policies. Projects involving *illegal activities, malicious software, fraud, harassment, or harmful content* may be disqualified.

### 10. **Judging Criteria**

Projects will be evaluated based on:
* **Innovation**
* Technical execution
* Problem and potential impact
* **Use of AI**
* User experience
* Scalability and potential

### 11. **Organizer’s Decision**

The organizers reserve the right to disqualify submissions that violate the **rules, eligibility requirements, or spirit of the hackathon**.
